competitorCoverage: Top-ranking articles about healthy eating for older adults generally cover the same core themes: nutrient needs change with age, protein and fiber become more important, hydration matters, and smaller or more frequent meals can help when appetite declines.[1][2][5][9][14] They also tend to include practical advice such as meal planning, budget-friendly choices, easy-to-prepare foods, and flags for common problems like unintentional weight loss, chewing difficulty, and dehydration.[2][9][16][18] To compete, a new article should add concrete portion guidance, symptom-based scenarios, and actionable food examples for common real-world barriers like low appetite, denture problems, dysphagia, medication timing, and living alone.[9][16][18]
